title: DinoTracker: AI classifies dinosaur footprints
summary: An unsupervised model trained on nearly 2,000 fossil footprints and millions of simulated variations identifies eight features of variation and agrees with experts about 90% of the time. Some tracks over 200 million years old resemble bird feet, which could suggest bird origins tens of millions of years earlier. The interpretation is open: they could be early dinosaurs whose feet happened to look similar.
organization: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin; and University of Edinburgh

evidence.tested: An unsupervised variational autoencoder was trained on 1,974 fossil footprints; after labeling, its groupings agreed with published expert identifications in 80-93% of cases (the press release says about 90%).
evidence.unknown: The interpretation is open: the tracks could be early dinosaurs whose feet resembled birds' feet; the study states no limitations section.
evidence.ai_role: An unsupervised disentangled variational autoencoder found eight shape-variation features without prior labels, and predicted which dinosaur made each track.
